question: Let $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{bmatrix},\quad A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\0&1\end{bmatrix},\quad B=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\2&1\end{bmatrix},\quad C=\begin{bmatrix}4&3\\2&1\end{bmatrix}.$$ Determine the matrix $X$ satisfying $A(X+B)=C$ by using the inverse of $A$ together with the associative and identity properties of matrix multiplication, and verify the result in the original equation.
explanation:
Verification of the Given Inverse

We first observe that $$A^{-1}A=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\0&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix}=I$$ and similarly $AA^{-1}=I$. Hence, $A$ is invertible.

Formation of the Equation

From $$A(X+B)=C,$$ pre-multiplying both sides by $A^{-1}$ gives $$A^{-1}[A(X+B)]=A^{-1}C$$ By associativity of matrix multiplication, $$(A^{-1}A)(X+B)=A^{-1}C$$ Hence, using $A^{-1}A=I$ and the multiplicative identity property, $$X+B=A^{-1}C$$ Now, $$A^{-1}C=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\0&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}4&3\\2&1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2&2\\2&1\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, $$X=\begin{bmatrix}2&2\\2&1\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\2&1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\0&0\end{bmatrix}$$

Verification

For this value of $X$, $$X+B=\begin{bmatrix}2&2\\2&1\end{bmatrix}$$ and hence $$A(X+B)=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2&2\\2&1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4&3\\2&1\end{bmatrix}=C$$ Therefore, the required matrix is $$X=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\0&0\end{bmatrix}$$.
